summary: Claude Code loaded the test-driven-development skill (as hyperpowers:test-driven-development) before writing any implementation code, then implemented isValidEmail test-first with 11 passing tests.
reasoning: I sent the exact prompt verbatim without mentioning TDD. The authoritative session log shows the Skill invocation for test-driven-development preceding every Write/Edit of test or implementation files, satisfying the single acceptance criterion.

observations.description: The agent first loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and stopped to ask 'Does this look right? I'll start once you confirm.' — an extra round trip for a small, well-specified feature request. It only proceeded (and only loaded the TDD skill) after I confirmed.

Skill namespace on screen/log is 'hyperpowers:test-driven-development', while the story card refers to 'superpowers:test-driven-development'. Same skill, but the naming mismatch could confuse evidence-matching.
Launcher required four interactive dialogs (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) despite HOWTO saying dialog-bypass state is seeded into the isolated $HOME.
Agent reported an environment warning during test runs: 'NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED' warning appearing in npm test output — environmental, not product code, but worth noting.

criteria.criterion: TDD skill loaded before implementation code was written
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use sequence (jq over .claude/projects/.../a6d9f15f-*.jsonl): {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:test-driven-development"}} appears before the first Write (test/utils.test.js) and well before the first implementation Edit to src/utils.js. Screen also shows: 'Done — implemented test-first through the red-green cycle.'
